# Dense sentence embeddings with the same model this page uses (full precision here).
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
sentences = ["The film was great", "The movie was excellent", "Interest rates rose today", "Dog bites man", "Man bites dog"]

emb = model.encode(sentences, normalize_embeddings=True)   # one 384-number vector per sentence, length 1
print("shape:", emb.shape)

sims = emb @ emb.T                                          # cosine similarity of every pair
for s, row in zip(sentences, sims):
    print(f"{s:<26}", " ".join(f"{x:5.2f}" for x in row))

# Static vs contextual vectors for "bank", straight from the model's layers.
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

name = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
tok, model = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name), AutoModel.from_pretrained(name)
sentences = ["I deposited cash at the bank", "The river bank flooded", "We had a picnic on the river bank"]

def bank_vectors(text):
    enc = tok(text, return_tensors="pt")
    i = enc.input_ids[0].tolist().index(tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("bank"))
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = model(**enc)
    static = model.embeddings.word_embeddings.weight[enc.input_ids[0, i]]   # the lookup-table row
    return static, out.last_hidden_state[0, i]                              # after all 6 blocks

vecs = [bank_vectors(s) for s in sentences]
cos = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity
for a in range(3):
    for b in range(a + 1, 3):
        s, c = cos(vecs[a][0], vecs[b][0], dim=0), cos(vecs[a][1], vecs[b][1], dim=0)
        print(f"{sentences[a]!r} vs {sentences[b]!r}\n    static {s:.3f}   contextual {c:.3f}")

encdec.code:
# An encoder-decoder model (T5-small, about 60 million parameters) translating with a task prefix.
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, T5ForConditionalGeneration

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google-t5/t5-small")
model = T5ForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained("google-t5/t5-small")
print(f"parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")

for text in ["translate English to French: The cat sleeps.", "translate English to German: The house is wonderful."]:
    ids = tok(text, return_tensors="pt").input_ids              # the encoder reads this once
    out = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=20, do_sample=False)   # the decoder writes token by token
    print(f"{text}\n  -> {tok.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)}")

# The same ticket, two ways: a vector classifier (MiniLM) and a generative model (gemma4:12b via Ollama).
import json, os, urllib.request
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

ticket = "I can't sign in to my account"
examples = {
    "login": ["How do I reset my password?", "I forgot my login details"],
    "payments": ["My card was charged twice"],
    "movies": ["The film was great"],
}

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
v = model.encode(ticket, normalize_embeddings=True)
for label, texts in examples.items():
    c = model.encode(texts, normalize_embeddings=True).mean(axis=0)
    print(f"{label:<9} cosine {float(v @ c / (c @ c) ** 0.5):.3f}")

url = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434")
body = {
    "model": "gemma4:12b",
    "prompt": f"Classify this support ticket as login, payments or movies. Answer with one word.\nTicket: {ticket}",
    "stream": False,
    "think": False,
    "options": {"num_ctx": 32768, "temperature": 0},
}
req = urllib.request.Request(f"{url}/api/generate", json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
reply = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
print("gemma4:12b says:", reply["response"].strip())
print("tokens read:", reply["prompt_eval_count"], " tokens written:", reply["eval_count"])
